questions.q: Which filter must every win rate report include?
questions.explain: Win rate is measured on closed deals only. Open opportunities are neither won nor lost and would distort the denominator.

questions.q: Why is it better to use the Won and Closed flags than to filter on a stage named 'Closed Won'?
options: The flags handle orgs with more than one won or lost stage and stay correct if stage names change
The flags are faster to type
Stage names are hidden from reports
questions.explain: The system flags follow the stage configuration, so the report survives renamed or additional won and lost stages.

questions.q: What does a summary formula of RowCount divided by PARENTGROUPVAL(RowCount, GRAND_SUMMARY) return for the Won row on closed deals?
options: The share of closed deals that were won, i.e. the win rate by count
questions.explain: Dividing each group's count by the grand total count gives that group's share of closed deals.

questions.q: Why show both count-based and value-based win rates?
options: Value-based is always the correct one
A team can win most small deals but lose the large ones, which count-based hides
questions.explain: The two measures answer different questions and can diverge sharply when deal sizes vary.

questions.q: Your org has no picklist field for why deals were lost. What is the best analyst response?
options: Summarize the free-text notes with a summary formula
Group by Stage and call it a loss reason
Flag the gap and recommend a required Loss Reason picklist, since free text cannot be reliably summarized
questions.explain: Reliable loss analysis needs a structured field. Raising the gap with your admin is the honest and useful move.
